findings.issue_text: HIGH — `lib/topic_retriever.rb` changed without corresponding tests or attached validation evidence.

MEDIUM — `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5-7`, `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5-7` — New endpoint specs only assert inheritance; CRUD, reassignment, migration, error handling, and host-specific import routing are unverified.

[lens/completeness][lens/architecture] CRITICAL — `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-15` — The migration dereferences the first site-setting query result before checking it exists. Default installations without persisted overrides can crash during upgrade before reaching the fallback.

[lens/architecture][lens/intent-preservation] HIGH — `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:24-25` — Legacy host values are inserted without normalization. Previously accepted URL/path entries remain verbatim but later lookups use only the hostname, disabling those embeds after upgrade.

HIGH — `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25` — Stored SQL injection: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates administrator-configurable legacy values directly into SQL, permitting arbitrary database statements during migration.
HIGH — `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2,14-17` — Validation permits `host:port`, but `URI#host` removes the port during lookup, so port-specific mappings can never match.
HIGH — `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14-17` — The query lowercases only the stored column, not the lookup hostname; uppercase input can fail the intended case-insensitive match.

[lens/architecture] HIGH — `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3-6`, `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17` — No case-insensitive unique index enforces one host-to-category mapping. Duplicate or case-variant rows can map a host differently, and unordered `.first` resolves them nondeterministically; the missing lookup index also causes sequential scans.

[lens/architecture] HIGH — `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:5`, `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:3`, `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:24` — No foreign key or category-existence validation prevents dangling mappings to nonexistent/deleted categories.

HIGH — `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192-201` — Generic hydration now treats every `*_ids` field as a sideloaded association and deletes the original IDs even when objects cannot be resolved, replacing valid IDs with `[undefined, …]` across unrelated REST models.
MEDIUM — `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:9-16` — Updating or deleting an unknown/stale ID dereferences `nil`, producing a 500 instead of a not-found response.

MEDIUM — `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:2,25,31` — Destructive data conversion uses irreversible SQL inside `change` and immediately deletes the old settings, preventing safe rollback and breaking compatibility with old instances during a rolling deployment.

LOW — `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb:1`, `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb:1` — Category and embeddable-host fabricator definitions were swapped into misleading filenames, creating unrelated churn and impairing discovery/loading.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HIGH — `lib/topic_retriever.rb` changed without corresponding tests or attached validation evidence.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that lib/topic_retriever.rb was changed from using SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? to EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?. Looking at the diff, there are corresponding tests added in spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb that test the EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? method. The finding claims there are no corresponding tests, but this is incorrect - the new EmbeddableHost model has tests for the host_allowed? method. The topic_retriever.rb change is a simple method call substitution that is covered by the new model's tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MEDIUM — `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5-7`, `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5-7` — New endpoint specs only assert inheritance; CRUD, reassignment, migration, error handling, and host-specific import routing are unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new controller specs only test inheritance (that the controllers are subclasses of AdminController) and don't test actual functionality like CRUD operations, error handling, or the migration logic. Looking at the diff, the specs at lines 5-7 in both files only contain `expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`. However, this is a test coverage concern/suggestion rather than a bug or defect in the actual code. The controllers themselves appear to be implemented correctly - the finding is about missing tests, not broken functionality. While more comprehensive tests would be beneficial, the lack of tests is not itself a 'bug, security issue, correctness problem, or clear defect the code introduces' - it's a code quality/coverage concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HIGH — `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25` — Stored SQL injection: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates administrator-configurable legacy values directly into SQL, permitting arbitrary database statements during migration.

adjudication.rationale: The migration code at line 25 does interpolate the variable `h` directly into an SQL string using string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. The value `h` comes from splitting the `embeddable_hosts` site setting value by newlines. While this is administrator-configurable data (not direct user input), it still represents a SQL injection vulnerability. If the stored setting contains malicious SQL (e.g., `'); DROP TABLE users; --`), it would be executed during migration. However, this is a migration that runs once during deployment, and the data source is a site setting that only administrators can modify. The risk is limited since administrators already have significant system access, but it's still technically a SQL injection vulnerability that could be exploited if an attacker gained admin access and set a malicious value before the migration runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HIGH — `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2,14-17` — Validation permits `host:port`, but `URI#host` removes the port during lookup, so port-specific mappings can never match.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in embeddable_host.rb: The validation regex on line 2 allows host:port format (:[0-9]{1,5}). The before_validation hook removes 'http://' and 'https://' prefixes and trailing paths, but does NOT remove the port. In record_for_host (lines 9-17), it uses URI(host) and then uri.host, which extracts just the hostname without the port. So if someone saves 'example.com:8080' as an embeddable host, the database stores 'example.com:8080', but when checking if a host is allowed via record_for_host('http://example.com:8080/page'), URI parses it and uri.host returns 'example.com' (without port), then the query 'WHERE lower(host) = example.com' won't match 'example.com:8080'. This is a real bug - port-specific hosts can be saved but will never match during lookup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/architecture] HIGH — `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3-6`, `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17` — No case-insensitive unique index enforces one host-to-category mapping. Duplicate or case-variant rows can map a host differently, and unordered `.first` resolves them nondeterministically; the missing lookup index also causes sequential scans.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real architectural issue. Looking at the migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3-6), the table is created with only `host` and `category_id` columns but no unique index on `host`. The model's `record_for_host` method (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17) uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` which would return nondeterministic results if duplicate hosts exist. Without a unique constraint, multiple rows with the same host (or case variants) could be inserted, and `.first` without explicit ordering would return unpredictable results. This is a legitimate data integrity and correctness concern - the code allows duplicate host entries which could map the same host to different categories, and the lookup behavior would be undefined.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/architecture] HIGH — `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:5`, `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:3`, `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:24` — No foreign key or category-existence validation prevents dangling mappings to nonexistent/deleted categories.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the migration creates embeddable_hosts table with category_id NOT NULL constraint. The EmbeddableHost model has 'belongs_to :category' but no validation for category existence. In the controller (save_host method), if category_id is blank, it defaults to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id. However, there's no foreign key constraint in the migration and no Rails validation to ensure the category actually exists. If a category is deleted, the embeddable_host records would have dangling references. This is a real data integrity issue - the code allows creating/updating embeddable_hosts with category_ids that may not exist, and doesn't handle category deletion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HIGH — `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192-201` — Generic hydration now treats every `*_ids` field as a sideloaded association and deletes the original IDs even when objects cannot be resolved, replacing valid IDs with `[undefined, …]` across unrelated REST models.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in store.js.es6, the new code handles `*_ids` fields (line 192-201). When `m[2]` is truthy (meaning it matched `_ids`), it maps over `obj[k]` calling `_lookupSubType` for each id. The result is assigned to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]` and the original key is deleted unconditionally (`delete obj[k]`). The issue is that `_lookupSubType` can return `undefined` if the subtype cannot be resolved from the root object. The code does `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` but `hydrated` is an array (from `.map()`), so it will never be falsy - it will be an array potentially containing `undefined` values. This means if IDs cannot be resolved, the original valid IDs are deleted and replaced with an array of `undefined` values. However, this is a generic store mechanism and the behavior for singular `_id` fields (lines 203-209) only deletes when hydration succeeds (`if (hydrated)`). The plural version doesn't have this guard, so it will always delete the original IDs even when hydration fails. This is a real behavioral difference that could cause data loss in the client-side model.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MEDIUM — `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:2,25,31` — Destructive data conversion uses irreversible SQL inside `change` and immediately deletes the old settings, preventing safe rollback and breaking compatibility with old instances during a rolling deployment.

adjudication.rationale: The migration uses `change` method but contains irreversible operations: it executes raw SQL to migrate data from site_settings to the new embeddable_hosts table, then deletes the original site_settings records with `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`. If a rollback is needed, the `change` method cannot automatically reverse these raw SQL operations, and the original data has been permanently deleted. This is a real problem because: 1) Using `change` implies reversibility but the migration is not reversible, 2) The DELETE statement permanently removes the old configuration data, making rollback impossible, 3) During rolling deployments, old instances would fail because the settings they depend on have been deleted.
